input.verdict: Mostly uninformative. Phase mp-504509 (I believe it is an Fe/V oxide, but I haven't checked its identity) has a predicted HSE gap of 2.75 eV. MEGNet overestimates the gaps of Fe-containing oxides; the Fe2O3 prediction of 2.77 eV is far above its roughly 2.1 eV experimental gap. Experimentally, Fe-V oxides absorb near 2.0-2.1 eV, so index 0 (Fe 0.44, V 0.43, low Bi) is the region most likely to absorb 602 nm light. I'm measuring it to contrast with the BiVO4-like anchor.

content.text:
I submitted **index 88** (Bi 0.35, Fe 0.23, V 0.42). It gave the highest photocurrent of the three compositions I measured. With only 3 of the library's 201 compositions measured, I don't know how close it is to the library's best.

| Index | Composition (Bi / Fe / V) | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 88 | 0.35 / 0.23 / 0.42 (near BiVO4 ratio, more Fe) | **7e-8 A** |
| 30 | 0.33 / 0.17 / 0.50 (BiVO4-like with some Fe) | 6e-8 A |
| 0 | 0.14 / 0.44 / 0.43 (Fe-V-rich, low Bi) | 2e-8 A |

- **How I picked the samples:** I chose them from general knowledge of these oxides, one in each main region. The third choice followed the trend in the first two measurements: Bi-V-rich beat Fe-V-rich, so I moved closer to a 1:1 Bi:V ratio and added Fe. The composition-based model suggestion (`gp_suggest`) also listed 88 among its top five.
- **The model tools didn't help rank candidates.**
  - The full phase list was too large to return, so I couldn't look up phase IDs. I had to guess them from memory, and some guesses weren't recognised.
  - The band-gap predictions were about 2.75 eV for both phases I tried, well above the 2.06 eV illumination. The model is known to overestimate gaps for Fe oxides (it gave 2.77 eV for Fe2O3, which is about 2.1 eV in practice). So I treated those predictions as uninformative, and the consultation notes I recorded before each measurement say so.
- **Not done:** I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so the phases present in the films are unconfirmed.
